fields.why: Opioid-prescription percentages and APCs are reported for each of the six NCHS urban-rural categories, an outcome measured per rurality group.
Rurality is the only SPD with 3 or more groups compared; period is not an SPD.

The 'lowest in large central metro (p<0.001)' and 'highest in noncore (p<0.02)' claims rest on multiplicity-adjusted Wald tests against named groups, not all pairs. The Table 2 Wald tests compare periods within each rurality level (rule 6: no entry), so the cross-group APC patterns are only side by side and the mechanical flag is a false alarm.
